assessment.why: Full recompute costs ~21% on H200. Sharded 26B states are ~52 GiB/GPU, so 4k-token activations should fit in 141 GB without recompute.
Compile pays off more on H200 (FSDP2 +24%). HF Trainer graph breaks and the HF stack overhead cut the gain; the main feasibility risk is a compile failure.
The 262k vocab makes the logits and cross-entropy large. Fused linear CE plus RMSNorm/RoPE/SwiGLU kernels cut glue-kernel time. Risk: the architecture may not be supported by Liger.
Recomputing 1/4 of layers recovers most of the 21% recompute tax. This only works if the harness honours every_n_layers; it is not a standard torch checkpoint kwarg.
Larger GEMMs and better amortised FSDP all-gathers per token. The memory headroom allows it. Note this doubles the global batch unless grad accumulation is lowered.
Skips the backward all-gather; NCCL is a large share of FSDP2 step time on H200. Cost: about 52 GB of full bf16 params held per GPU, which is tight next to the states.
The fused AdamW kernel on about 3.2B sharded params per GPU saves tens of ms against a step of several seconds. Small, but above the 0.14% noise.
FSDP reduce-scatters every micro-batch anyway, so accumulation saves no communication. Running the optimizer step twice as often per token slows token throughput slightly.
Mainly reduces fragmentation and allocator retries. Speed only moves if memory gets tight, for example with recompute off or noreshard.
FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter are mostly overlapped with compute. Disabling NVLS frees a little memory and may slightly slow the exposed collectives.
Training is in bf16, so almost no fp32 matmuls are left for TF32 to accelerate.
Steps take seconds on a 26B model with 4k sequences; two workers already hide tokenised-batch loading.

calls.memory_note: At 25.81B params, FSDP across 8 GPUs puts fp32 params, grads and Adam states at about 52 GiB per GPU, leaving roughly 80 GiB for activations and the 262k-vocab logits; that should allow recompute off at mbs 1, with Liger shrinking the logits, while noreshard plus mbs 2 is the tight combination.

findings.issue: Every decoder layer is checkpointed (gradient_checkpointing=true, every_n_layers=1). The whole forward runs twice per micro-batch, roughly 25-33% extra compute inside the 3.1 s compute phase. With 141 GiB per GPU, FSDP sharding over 8 GPUs and 1x4096 tokens per micro-batch, there is likely room to r

The LM head builds the full [tokens x vocab] logits, upcasts them to fp32 and then runs cross-entropy. That is a large memory-bound kernel chain and a big activation for a ~150-250k vocab. RMSNorm, SwiGLU and RoPE also run as separate element-wise kernels. Liger's fused linear-cross-entropy and fuse
Element-wise work between matmuls (activations, residual adds, norms, dtype casts) is not fused in eager mode.
The optimizer is adamw_torch with a foreach, non-fused update over the FSDP shards. This is the 61.6 ms optimizer phase.

Two micro-batches of 1 run per update (gradient_accumulation_steps=2). Each pays its own FSDP all-gather and reduce-scatter and gets lower GEMM occupancy. per_device_train_batch_size=2 with gradient_accumulation_steps=1 keeps global_batch=16 and halves the collective count.
FSDP reshards parameters after forward, so each micro-batch all-gathers them again in backward and again for recompute. The no-reshard config keeps the gathered parameters.

Trainer's logging_nan_inf_filter evaluates torch.isnan/isinf on the loss as a Python bool after every micro-step. That is a host-device sync per micro-batch, but the GPU queue has nearly drained after backward by then, so the exposed cost is well under 1% of the step. It is not worth a test run.
Each sample does np.array copies and a torch.cat in __getitem__. This runs in 2 dataloader workers with pinned memory, so it is off the critical path.
Memory fragmentation and allocator churn under recompute and FSDP all-gathers cost a little on every phase.

hypotheses.mechanism: partial_recompute_every_2_layers
hypotheses.rationale: Compute is 92% of the update, and full recompute costs about 21% on H200 (rule H7). Checkpointing every 2nd layer removes about half the recomputed forward passes. Activation memory rises from about 13 GiB to roughly 40 GiB. The FSDP-sharded weights, grads and optimizer states are about 48 GiB per GPU (the accounting term of 384.6 GiB is unsharded), so this fits in 141 GiB.

hypotheses.mechanism: partial_recompute_every_3_layers
hypotheses.rationale: This recomputes only one layer in three, so it recovers about two thirds of the recompute tax on the dominant compute phase. Peak activation memory grows further but should still fit alongside about 48 GiB of sharded state.

hypotheses.mechanism: partial_recompute_every_4_layers
hypotheses.rationale: This recomputes only one layer in four, which comes close to the gain of disabling checkpointing (already queued from experience) at lower memory. The 262k-vocab logits (6 GiB) and MoE routing buffers add some OOM risk.

hypotheses.mechanism: larger_microbatch_no_accumulation
hypotheses.rationale: The global batch stays at 16 (8 GPUs x 2 x 1). This halves the number of micro-steps, so FSDP all-gathers, reduce-scatters, per-step launch overhead and HF MoE routing glue run once instead of twice. GEMMs and expert batches also get larger, and the job is overhead-bound under HF MoE (rule H6). Activations double, but checkpointing keeps them at about 26 GiB.

hypotheses.mechanism: fsdp_no_reshard_after_forward
hypotheses.rationale: Keeping parameters gathered after forward removes the backward all-gather, and with GA=2 also the repeated gathers per micro-step. Communication on H200 tends to hide inside the compute phase (rule H15). Unsharded bf16 parameters add about 48 GiB per GPU, which is near but within capacity.

hypotheses.mechanism: expandable_segments_allocator
hypotheses.rationale: This reduces fragmentation and cudaMalloc/free churn from variable-size MoE dispatch buffers and recompute. It should mostly shrink the residual (about 4%) and allocator stalls inside compute.

hypotheses.mechanism: tf32_matmul
hypotheses.rationale: TF32 only speeds up fp32 matmuls, such as fp32 router or gating GEMMs and fp32 norm or logit upcasts. The bulk of the model is bf16, so the gain is small. The loss effect is well inside the 3% tolerance.

hypotheses.mechanism: disable_nvls
hypotheses.rationale: NVLS collectives use SM-light switch reductions but can carry setup and registration overhead for many mid-size FSDP collectives. Ring or tree algorithms may be faster here. The comm phase is only 2%, which bounds the gain.

hypotheses.mechanism: more_dataloader_workers
hypotheses.rationale: Prefetching more batches could hide any input stall inside the residual phase. With 3.4 s per update, 2 workers are probably sufficient, so the expected gain is small.

hypotheses.mechanism: partial_recompute_every_2_layers_at_mbs2
hypotheses.rationale: The earlier every_n_layers tests (c1 and c3, -0.35 %) ran at mbs1 with accumulation 2. At mbs2 the per-layer GEMMs are larger and the job is 92 % compute, so skipping half of the recompute forwards could save up to about 10 % of compute. The flat mbs1 result suggests the kwarg may only partly change what is recomputed. Activation memory at mbs2 roughly doubles, which is a moderate OOM risk.

hypotheses.mechanism: partial_recompute_every_4_layers_with_expandable_segments
hypotheses.rationale: every_n_layers 4 crashed in c2 (completes / no_errors failed), likely from memory fragmentation or OOM. Expandable segments reduce fragmentation and may let the larger saved-activation footprint fit. If it fits, about 75 % of the recompute forwards are removed. At mbs2 the footprint is larger than in c2, so feasibility is low.

hypotheses.mechanism: partial_recompute_every_3_layers_at_mbs2
hypotheses.rationale: This is the same mechanism as every_n_layers 2 but recomputes fewer layers. It has not been tested at the mbs2 incumbent. It saves more recompute than every 2 layers and needs more activation memory than it does.

hypotheses.mechanism: max_dataloader_workers
hypotheses.rationale: The residual phase is 4.4 % (150 ms) and may include input stalls at mbs2. Eight workers prefetch further ahead than the queued 4-worker test; any gain is capped by the residual.

hypotheses.mechanism: no_pin_memory
hypotheses.rationale: Unpinned memory removes the pin-thread contention with the host but makes host-to-device copies synchronous. With only 2x4096 tokens per GPU per step, the copy is negligible, so the net effect is expected near zero. This is a low-value probe of the residual.

assessment.why: Full recompute costs about 21% on H200 (H7). About 52 GiB/GPU of sharded fp32 state leaves room for activations at seq 4k mbs1. Risk: 25.8B params don't match the listed dims.
Vocab 262k gives about 10 GiB of fp32 logits at 4k; fused CE skips materializing them. Glue kernels matter on H200 (H15). It is a no-op if the arch is unsupported.
H200 compile wins are large (FSDP2 +24%, H12), but HF Trainer adds graph breaks with FSDP2 and checkpointing, so expect less. There is compile/graph-break risk.
Halving recompute recovers about half of the 21% tax (H7). Risk: if the harness forwards the kwarg to torch checkpoint unhandled, it is ignored (0) or rejected.
Larger micro-batch amortizes FSDP gathers and glue per token (H15). Logits double to about 20 GiB but fit. Doubles the global batch unless GA is cut to 1.
Skips the backward all-gather (NCCL is about 28% of FSDP2 kernel time, H15) but holds about 52 GB of unsharded bf16 params. Tight if combined with no recompute.
3.2B params/GPU optimizer step is only tens of ms against a step of seconds, so the gain is small but real. Fused AdamW supports DTensor.
FSDP2 gathers per micro-step anyway; the optimizer is a negligible share. Alone it only halves the global batch. Pair it with mbs 2 to keep the batch.
Reduces fragmentation and cudaMalloc retries. It helps feasibility of the memory-heavy combos more than speed at this headroom.
Disabling NVSwitch SHARP removes a faster path for reduce-scatter/all-reduce. Comms are a large share on H200 FSDP2 (H15).
Steps take seconds at 25.8B; 2 workers already keep up with tokenized 4k batches.
Matmuls run in bf16; only stray fp32 matmuls are affected.

calls.memory_note: Full fine-tuning under FSDP2 on 8 GPUs puts about 52 GiB/GPU in sharded fp32 params, grads and Adam, plus about 10 GiB of 262k-vocab logits, leaving roughly 70 GiB for activations; no recompute plus noreshard (+52 GB) is the one combination likely to approach the 141 GB limit.

findings.issue: Gradient checkpointing on every layer (every_n_layers=1) re-runs the full forward of each decoder layer in backward, roughly +25-33% of the compute phase. Memory headroom (1.7B params, FSDP over 8x141 GiB, seq 4096) allows turning it off or checkpointing fewer layers.

The LM head plus HF ForCausalLMLoss materialises 4096x~151k logits and upcasts them to fp32 for cross-entropy. This is a large memory and bandwidth cost per micro-batch, and RMSNorm, SwiGLU and RoPE are unfused element-wise ops.
Eager per-op execution of element-wise and norm work in the decoder layers adds kernel-launch and memory-traffic overhead inside the compute phase.
The model dtype follows targs.bf16. Any fp32 matmuls (or fp32 parts such as the loss and norms) run at full fp32 precision while tf32 is off.
AdamW uses the for-each (non-fused) implementation, about 61 ms per update; a multi-tensor fused kernel shortens it.
Large, variable-size activation and logit buffers under the default caching allocator can fragment memory and cause allocator retries or cudaMalloc calls per step.

FSDP2 reshards parameters after forward and all-gathers them again in backward on each of the 2 accumulation micro-steps. This is small (comm 1.6%) but avoidable with no-reshard or a single micro-step (batch 2 x accum 1 keeps global_batch=16).

PackedSFT.__getitem__ copies from the memmap via np.array and builds labels with torch.cat for every sample. This is cheap and runs in dataloader workers with pinned memory, so it is off the critical path.

hypotheses.mechanism: larger micro-batch, one micro-step per update (mbs 2 x GA 1 x DP 8 = 16)
hypotheses.rationale: Compute is 92% of the update. The accounting note says this is an MoE, and HF MoE expert GEMMs with mbs 1 are small and launch-bound. Doubling the tokens per micro-step raises GEMM efficiency. It also halves the per-micro-step FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter rounds and the Python/launch overhead. Global batch stays 16. With full recompute the extra activations are only a few GiB, so memory is safe.

hypotheses.mechanism: selective recompute: checkpoint every 2nd layer
hypotheses.rationale: Full recompute costs about 21% on H200 (rule H7). Recomputing half the layers recovers about half of that. Activations are only about 13 GiB at full recompute, so keeping half the layers' activations fits in 141 GiB. The fully-off variant is already queued; this is the lower-memory middle point.

hypotheses.mechanism: selective recompute: checkpoint every 4th layer
hypotheses.rationale: This recomputes only 1/4 of the 30 layers, recovering about 3/4 of the roughly 21% recompute tax. Memory rises with the stored activations; it fits only if the sharded states are near the expected ~52 GiB per GPU and not the 384 GiB closed-form figure (which looks unsharded).

hypotheses.mechanism: FSDP2 no reshard after forward (no re-all-gather in backward)
hypotheses.rationale: Keeping unsharded bf16 params between forward and backward removes one all-gather per layer per micro-step. With recompute, the checkpointed forward otherwise all-gathers again. Comm is only 1.6% exposed, but the all-gather launches also delay compute streams. The cost is about 52 GB of resident bf16 params per GPU, which is a memory risk.

hypotheses.mechanism: expandable segments allocator
hypotheses.rationale: This reduces fragmentation and cudaMalloc/free churn from variable MoE routing shapes and FSDP buffers. It acts on every phase and is small but cheap to test.

hypotheses.mechanism: TF32 for remaining fp32 matmuls
hypotheses.rationale: Main GEMMs are bf16. However, the router, norm upcasts and any fp32 logits or loss matmuls (vocab 262k) would run at 347 vs 51 TFLOPS. Phase targets list tf32 for the compute phase. The loss change should be well within 3%.

hypotheses.mechanism: disable NVLS collectives
hypotheses.rationale: Phase targets list NVLS for compute. NVLS uses SM-side multicast and reserves memory and channels. Ring/tree all-gather may interfere less with the overlapped compute. The effect is bounded by the small comm share.

hypotheses.mechanism: more dataloader workers
hypotheses.rationale: Residual is 4.5% of the update. Part of it may be host-side batch preparation with 2 workers at seq 4096. The gain is at most a fraction of the residual.

hypotheses.mechanism: grouped-GEMM MoE experts instead of HF per-expert loop
hypotheses.rationale: Rule H6: HF-implemented MoE is overhead-bound (1.39-2.11x only vs H20). Python loops over experts with tiny GEMMs and index_select/index_add dominate compute, which is 92% of the update. Grouped GEMM removes per-expert launches and host syncs. The arithmetic is identical up to summation order. It is risky because module names must match the installed transformers version.

hypotheses.mechanism: force fused SDPA attention backend (cuDNN/flash) instead of eager/math
hypotheses.rationale: Gemma-family models often default to eager attention. At seq 4096 with 16 heads, eager materializes 4096x4096 scores per head, forward and again in recompute. cuDNN SDPA on H200 is much faster and saves memory. If the model is already on SDPA, the patch is a no-op apart from the backend preference.

hypotheses.mechanism: chunked/fused cross-entropy over 262k vocab without full fp32 logits
hypotheses.rationale: The 262k vocab gives 6 GiB of logits plus fp32 upcast copies and the softmax backward per micro-step. These are memory-bandwidth-bound elementwise passes. Chunking removes the large fp32 materialization. This overlaps partly with the queued Liger test (fused linear CE), but it applies to the model regardless of Liger's model support.

hypotheses.mechanism: selective recompute: checkpoint every 3rd layer
hypotheses.rationale: Compute is 92% of the update, and full recompute adds a second forward pass (H7: full recompute costs about 21%). hypotheses.mechanism: selective recompute every 4th layer, with the expandable-segments allocator so it fits

hypotheses.mechanism: no recompute, enabled by the expandable-segments allocator

hypotheses.mechanism: no recompute at micro-batch 1 x GA 2 (smaller micro-batch enables dropping recompute)

hypotheses.mechanism: more dataloader workers (8)
hypotheses.rationale: Part of the 150 ms residual may be exposed host-side batch preparation. Eight workers prefetch further ahead than the queued 4. The gain is bounded by the residual, which is 4.5% of the update.

hypotheses.mechanism: disable pinned host memory for the dataloader
hypotheses.rationale: With very small token batches, the pin-memory thread can add host overhead and synchronization. The expected effect is near zero and is bounded by the residual phase.

assessment.why: H200 full-recompute tax is about 21% (H7). About 52 GB/GPU of sharded state leaves room for mbs1 s4k activations without recompute (H5). The 262k-vocab logits are the main memory risk.
The 262k vocab gives about 4 GB fp32 logits per microbatch; fused linear-CE removes them and the glue kernels, which matter on H200 (H15). If the model type is unsupported, Liger is a no-op.
H200 rule says always compile (FSDP2 +24%). HF Trainer models have more graph breaks than titan, and HF is overhead-bound (H6), so expect a smaller gain.
Recomputes half the layers, recovering about half of the 21% recompute tax. Fallback if fully disabling checkpointing OOMs.
FSDP2 NCCL is about 28% of H200 step time (H15); mbs2 halves the 52 GB all-gathers per token. Global batch doubles to 32.
Saves the backward re-gather, but keeps about 52 GB of unsharded bf16 params per GPU. Fits only with recompute kept on.
3.2B sharded params/GPU: the step is tens of ms against a multi-second step. Small gain but above the 0.14% noise.
Less fragmentation from the large logits and gather buffers. Mainly buys memory headroom, not speed.
bf16 autocast leaves almost no fp32 matmuls (tf32 is 347 vs bf16 662 TFLOPS); only stray fp32 ops benefit.
NVLS helps NVSwitch collectives. Disabling frees some buffer memory but can slightly slow the FSDP all-gather and reduce-scatter.
Step is several seconds for 8k tokens/GPU; 2 workers already hide loading.
Alone it halves global batch to 8, amortizing the optimizer step over fewer tokens. Pair it with mbs2 to keep global batch at 16.

calls.memory_note: About 52 GB/GPU of sharded fp32 params, grads and Adam states leaves about 85 GB at mbs1 with recompute; dropping recompute (Liger removes the 262k-vocab logits) should fit, but adding mbs2 or noreshard (+52 GB) on top risks OOM.

findings.issue: The model dtype comes from targs.bf16. A 1.7B model at 2x4096 tokens per GPU taking about 3.1 s of compute (about 110 TFLOP of work including recompute) points to fp32 matmuls without TF32, the slow GEMM path. The phase targets name tf32 for the compute phase.

The LM head and cross-entropy build full [4096 x vocab] logits per micro-batch (vocab of about 152k, roughly 2.5 GB in fp32) and upcast them, which adds memory-bound kernels and large allocations every micro-step. A fused linear + cross-entropy removes this.

Gradient checkpointing on every layer recomputes the whole forward in backward, about a third more compute. With 141 GiB per GPU and per-device batch 1, part or all of this recompute can likely be dropped.
Eager-mode RMSNorm, rotary embeddings and SwiGLU launch many unfused element-wise kernels per layer.
The non-fused AdamW runs a per-parameter loop over the sharded parameters. This is small at 1.8% of the update.
PackedSFT.__getitem__ copies from memmap and does a torch.cat on the host for each sample. With 2 workers and 2 samples per GPU per 3.4 s step, this is off the critical path.

hypotheses.mechanism: selective activation recompute: checkpoint every 2nd decoder layer instead of every layer, so half the layers skip the forward recompute
hypotheses.rationale: Compute is 92% of the update, and full recompute adds about one extra forward pass (around 21% tax on H200 per rule H7). Halving the recompute should recover roughly half of that. Keeping activations for 15 more layers at seq 4096, mbs 1, costs well under the 67 GiB margin. The queued experience test only covers the full on/off switch, not this setting.

hypotheses.mechanism: lighter selective recompute: checkpoint every 4th layer, so about 3/4 of layers keep their activations
hypotheses.rationale: This removes about 75% of the recompute forward, which sits in the 92% compute phase. It is a fallback if dropping checkpointing entirely runs out of memory or thrashes. Its memory cost lies between every_n=2 and no checkpointing.

hypotheses.mechanism: intermediate selective recompute: checkpoint every 3rd layer
hypotheses.rationale: This removes about 2/3 of the recompute cost, at memory between the 2 and 4 settings. It gives a monotone point that helps the search locate the memory/speed edge.

hypotheses.mechanism: one micro-batch of 2 instead of two micro-batches of 1 (same global batch 16): halves the per-update FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter rounds and kernel launches, and doubles tokens per GEMM, which helps
hypotheses.rationale: The model looks like an HF-implemented MoE: 25.8B parameters with a small hidden size, and accounting flags unknown experts. Such models are launch- and overhead-bound (rule H6), so larger per-expert token batches and half as many forward/backward passes cut the fixed costs. FSDP2 also gathers and reduce-scatters parameters once instead of twice. Activations and the 262k-vocab logits double, addin

hypotheses.mechanism: FSDP2 without resharding after forward: keep the gathered parameters through backward to skip the backward all-gather
hypotheses.rationale: Comm is 2.2% exposed, but all-gathers also contend with compute through SM and HBM use. With gradient checkpointing, the recompute plus backward each need the gathered weights, so not resharding saves one all-gather per micro-batch. Unsharded bf16 weights are about 48 GiB versus 6 GiB sharded, so this needs most of the 67 GiB margin. That makes it risky and a candidate for a memory probe.

hypotheses.mechanism: TF32 for the remaining fp32 matmuls (router, fp32 upcasts, loss parts)
hypotheses.rationale: phase_targets names tf32 for the compute phase. The bulk of the GEMMs are bf16, but MoE routers and some fp32 upcast paths run fp32 matmuls at 51 vs 347 TFLOPS. The gain is small unless such paths exist; loss impact is negligible.

hypotheses.mechanism: expandable_segments allocator to cut fragmentation and cudaMalloc/free churn
hypotheses.rationale: FSDP2 all-gather buffers and the variable MoE expert token counts produce varying tensor sizes, which cause allocator churn. Expandable segments reduce this churn and the residual (4% of the update). They also free slack that helps the memory-spending moves.

hypotheses.mechanism: disable NVLink SHARP (NVLS) for the FSDP collectives

assessment.why: Recompute is ~25% of step at 6.7 TFLOP/GPU per microbatch on H100; halving it helps. 77.3 GiB holds no 35B-model activation tests, so memory is unproven.
Vocab 248k x 8k tokens: fused linear cross-entropy skips 4-8 GB of logits and their time; fused RMSNorm/SwiGLU/RoPE help too. Risk: model family may lack a Liger patch.
Compute-bound on H100 (740 TF), so fusion helps. FSDP2, checkpointing and HF graph breaks under compile often fail or recompile; untested.
Fused Adam over a ~2.2B-param shard per GPU saves part of the optimizer step; small share of a multi-second step.
Amortizes the optimizer step over 2 microbatches; FSDP2 all-gathers still repeat each microbatch. Doubles global batch, so tokens/s is the metric.
Speed-neutral; cuts FSDP2 fragmentation and adds headroom, so it is useful alongside less checkpointing.
2-node IB: FSDP gathers/scatters ~200 GB/GPU per microbatch, mostly overlapped. More channels may lift IB use but take SMs from compute.
bf16 training: almost no fp32 matmuls are left for TF32 to speed up.
Pre-tokenized 4k text at a multi-second step: 2 workers already keep up.
Turns off NVLink SHARP for intra-node collectives on H100. It frees some NCCL buffer memory but slows gather/scatter a little.
Halves tokens per FSDP all-gather (same comm volume per microbatch), so comm share doubles on 2-node IB. Only use it as a memory fallback.
No reshard keeps all unsharded bf16 params (~70 GB for 35B) through backward, on top of the sharded state. OOM at 77.3 GiB.

calls.memory_note: Full fine-tune with FSDP2 over 16 GPUs uses ~35 GB per GPU for sharded fp32 params, grads and Adam, plus a few GB of layer gather buffers and up to 8 GB of 248k-vocab logits. That leaves roughly 25-30 GiB for activations, so every_n_layers=2 fits only if Liger removes the logits and the per-layer MLP activations are moderate (if the run is LoRA, headroom is far larger).

Each layer runs an unfused depthwise nn.Conv1d with padding, a slice and a separate SiLU over a tensor of about 2 x 8192 x 4096 bf16. This happens in forward, in
The model runs with unfused RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE and cross-entropy, and the HF loss materialises the full-vocabulary logits.
The optimizer step uses the multi-kernel adamw_torch, about 3% of the update.
Every layer is recomputed under full gradient checkpointing, which costs about one extra forward of compute.
Each sample does a per-item torch.cat and an int64 copy in __getitem__. This is off the critical path with 2 workers and pinned memory, so the cost is negligible.

hypotheses.mechanism: MoE experts via grouped GEMM (transformers experts_implementation='grouped_mm') instead of the per-expert eager loop
hypotheses.rationale: This looks like Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: hidden 2048, 40 layers, vocab 248k, and the accounting flags it as MoE. About 3B params are active and each GPU sees 8192 tokens, so the ideal compute is roughly 0.3 s per update. Measured compute is 1.71 s. A large part of that gap fits an eager per-expert loop: many tiny GEMMs, index_add calls and a nonzero/where sync per expert. It runs in forward, again in reco

hypotheses.mechanism: Checkpoint only every 3rd layer (less recompute)
hypotheses.rationale: Full recompute adds about one forward pass, roughly 25% of compute. Dropping two thirds of it should save about 15% of the 1712 ms compute phase. Weights, grads and bf16 Adam state for 35B on DP8 come to about 35 GB. That leaves room for roughly 27 non-checkpointed layers of about 1 GB each at 8192 tokens, but it is tight.

hypotheses.mechanism: Checkpoint only every 4th layer
hypotheses.rationale: This removes 3/4 of the recompute forward, so the saving is larger than with n=3. The cost is 30 layers of stored activations, plus about 5.7 GB of logits and FSDP all-gather buffers. OOM risk is meaningful.

hypotheses.mechanism: Smaller micro-batch to enable much less recompute (mbs1 x GA2, keeping global batch 16, with every 4th layer checkpointed)
hypotheses.rationale: Halving the micro-batch halves activation memory, so dropping most of the recompute fits safely. That saves about 17% of compute. Against that, the FSDP all-gather and reduce-scatter run twice per update, adding about 85 ms. The smaller GEMMs and the per-micro-batch overhead also cost a few percent.

hypotheses.mechanism: torch.compile the model (fuse element-wise, norm and router glue)
hypotheses.rationale: Many small unfused ops sit around the GDN, MoE routing and norms. Compile could fuse them. However, data-dependent MoE shapes, fla Triton kernels, FSDP2 and checkpointing all invite graph breaks, recompiles or crashes.

hypotheses.mechanism: Expandable-segments allocator
hypotheses.rationale: MoE token counts per expert vary every step. Together with the 8 GB logits and FSDP buffers, this fragments the caching allocator and can trigger cudaFree/malloc retries. Expandable segments removes most of that cost.

hypotheses.mechanism: Disable NVLS collectives
hypotheses.rationale: Comm is 84.5 ms and partly overlapped. Across two nodes over IB, NVLS/NVLS-tree may not be the best algorithm, and it takes SM and memory resources. The effect is small either way.

hypotheses.mechanism: More NCCL channels for inter-node FSDP collectives
hypotheses.rationale: More channels can raise IB reduce-scatter and all-gather throughput for the 4.5% comm phase. Each extra channel takes SMs from overlapped compute, so the net effect is near zero.

hypotheses.mechanism: Keep parameters unsharded after forward (no backward all-gather)
hypotheses.rationale: This saves the backward re-gather, roughly a third of FSDP traffic. But holding all 35B bf16 params (about 70 GB) gathered between forward and backward almost certainly OOMs on 77 GB.

hypotheses.mechanism: Prefer cuDNN then flash SDPA for the full-attention layers (head_dim 256, GQA)
hypotheses.rationale: Only about 10 of the 40 layers are full attention, at roughly 40 ms total. The cuDNN Hopper kernels for d=256 beat FA2 by maybe 1.3-1.5x. Setting a priority rather than forcing one backend keeps unsupported shapes, such as GQA without cuDNN support, working.

hypotheses.mechanism: TF32 for any fp32 matmuls
hypotheses.rationale: The model runs in bf16, so only stray fp32 GEMMs (router or loss upcasts, if any) are affected. The gain is likely negligible.

hypotheses.mechanism: Recompute only every 3rd layer, using expandable-segments allocation so it fits in memory
hypotheses.rationale: Compute is 91% of the update, and full recompute adds roughly one extra forward pass. Dropping 2/3 of that recompute is worth more than 10%. c2 (every_n_layers 3 alone) and c4 failed to complete, most likely from OOM or fragmentation at peak in the backward pass. Expandable segments remove fragmentation slack (several GiB with FSDP2 all-gather buffers plus variable-size MoE expert intermediates),

hypotheses.mechanism: Deeper FSDP2 prefetch: all-gather the next 2 decoder layers ahead in forward and backward instead of the implicit 1
hypotheses.rationale: Each 35B MoE decoder layer gathers about 1.7 GB of bf16 parameters over IB across 2 nodes, while its compute is small (3B active). The per-update traffic (~210 GB, lower bound 0.73 s) is mostly hidden, but 84 ms of comm stays exposed. That exposed part grows as compute shrinks. Prefetching 2 layers deep hides gather latency spikes. FSDP2 skips its forward hooks during checkpoint recompute (PRE_BAC

hypotheses.mechanism: Regional torch.compile of the Qwen3.5 RMSNorm modules only (fuse fp32 cast, pow, mean, rsqrt, (1+w) scale and cast into one kernel)
hypotheses.rationale: Every layer runs 2 hidden-size norms on 8192x2048 tokens in eager mode as about 7 separate kernels over fp32 copies. The 10 attention layers add q/k norms. Each runs in forward, in recompute and in backward. Fusing them saves tens of ms of HBM traffic and many launches in a job that looks launch-heavy (MFU far below ideal). The scope is narrow on purpose: it avoids the MoE data-dependent graph bre

hypotheses.mechanism: Fewer Python garbage-collector passes during the launch-bound step
hypotheses.rationale: The eager MoE expert loop (256 experts, 40 layers, run in forward, recompute and backward) creates very many Python tensor wrappers per step. At the default 700-allocation threshold, frequent gen-0 and periodic full collections stall the host thread that feeds the GPU. With update time far above the FLOP ideal, host overhead is on the critical path. No arithmetic changes. Memory risk is negligible

hypotheses.mechanism: Bind each rank's main thread and dataloader workers to the CPU cores local to its GPU's NUMA node
hypotheses.rationale: The step looks host-launch-bound: many small MoE expert kernels and per-expert index syncs, at roughly 15% of FLOP ideal. Unbound ranks can migrate across sockets, which adds remote-memory latency to kernel launches, sync polling and pinned-memory copies. The patch pins each rank to its GPU's local cores, using the PCI order of NVIDIA 3D controllers. It skips itself when CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES remap

assessment.why: The 248k vocab at mbs2 x 4096 gives about 8 GB of fp32 logits plus their grads; fused linear-CE removes them. Feasibility depends on Liger supporting this architecture (shape looks like Qwen3.5-35B-A3B).
Halves the recompute (about 1/8 of compute). Memory risk: if the FFN is truly dense (~137k intermediate implied), 20 uncheckpointed layers OOM. If MoE (A3B-like), it adds ~10 GB.
About 2.2B sharded params per GPU (35B/16); a fused step replaces the multi-kernel foreach Adam. Small share of a 2-node step.
Variable-size FSDP2 all-gather buffers and large logits fragment the 79.6 GB H100. Expandable segments avoid cudaMalloc retries and add headroom.
Under HF Trainer, FSDP2 plus checkpointing plus a possible MoE expert loop or linear-attention kernels cause graph breaks and recompiles. Gain is uncertain; first compile is long on 16 ranks.
Amortizes the optimizer step over 2 micro-batches per sample. FSDP2 still reduce-scatters every micro-step. Changes the global batch (B12).
NVLS speeds intra-node collectives on H100 NVSwitch, but at 2 nodes IB scaling is near-perfect (x0.98-1.0). Disabling frees some memory but may slow the all-gather slightly.
FSDP traffic at 2 nodes is already well overlapped on this IB fabric. More channels take SMs from compute.
Training matmuls run in bf16; TF32 only touches the few fp32 matmuls (e.g. an upcast loss), which are negligible.
Tokenized 4k sequences need little CPU per step; a multi-second 35B step hides loading at 2 workers. Measure the median step to avoid epoch stalls.
Smaller GEMMs and the same per-step FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter at half the tokens lower throughput. Useful only as a memory fallback.
No reshard keeps every layer's unsharded bf16 weights until backward: 35B x 2 B = 70 GB per GPU on top of optimizer state, which exceeds 79.6 GB.

calls.memory_note: Assuming full fine-tuning, fp32 params, grads and Adam state sharded over 16 GPUs take about 35 GB, plus about 16 GB of fp32 logits and grads from the 248k vocab (removed by Liger) and recompute buffers, leaving roughly 15-25 GB headroom. That headroom is enough for every_n_layers 2 only if the model is MoE-like (A3B shape), never enough for no-reshard FSDP.

The LM head materializes the full bf16 logits for 2x4096 tokens over the roughly 248k-token vocabulary, then upcasts them to fp32 for the cross-entropy. This is large memory traffic and allocation on every step, and its backward is as large.
AdamW runs as the foreach (unfused) implementation over the FSDP shards. This is the optimizer phase, 3% of the update.
Gradient checkpointing on every layer recomputes the whole forward, roughly a third of compute. With 77 GiB per GPU and FSDP, checkpointing fewer layers may fit in memory.

hypotheses.mechanism: Checkpoint every 2nd layer instead of every layer
hypotheses.rationale: Full recompute costs about one forward pass, roughly 25-30% of the 1712 ms of compute. Halving it saves about 200 ms. FSDP-sharded bf16 weights and optimizer state take about 35 GB per GPU. Activations for 20 un-checkpointed MoE layers at 2x4096 tokens could add 25-35 GB, so OOM is a real risk.

hypotheses.mechanism: Checkpoint every 3rd layer
hypotheses.rationale: Removes about 2/3 of the recompute forward pass. It needs roughly 27 layers' full activations, so memory is the main risk.

hypotheses.mechanism: Checkpoint every 4th layer
hypotheses.rationale: Removes about 3/4 of the recompute. It needs about 30 layers' activations, so OOM is likely at mbs 2 and seq 4096, but the gain is largest if it fits.

hypotheses.mechanism: torch.compile of the model (fused element-wise work, norms, gates, router)
hypotheses.rationale: The gated-DeltaNet and MoE layers carry a lot of unfused element-wise work (gates, SiLU, RMSNorm-gated, routing softmax/topk), which compile can fuse. Risks: graph breaks around fla Triton kernels, data-dependent MoE routing, FSDP2 hooks and checkpointing, plus compile time eating into the measured window.

hypotheses.mechanism: cuDNN SDPA first in the backend priority for the full-attention layers
hypotheses.rationale: On H100 the cuDNN attention backend beats the flash-v2 SDPA backend by about 1.2-1.5x at seq 4096 with GQA. Setting it as priority rather than forcing it lets unsupported calls fall back. Only the full-attention layers (about 1/4 of the 40) use SDPA, so the gain is small.

hypotheses.mechanism: Keep parameters unsharded after forward (no backward re-all-gather)
hypotheses.rationale: Removes the backward all-gather, roughly half of the parameter traffic over IB, cutting the exposed comm (87 ms) and contention with compute. However, keeping 35B bf16 parameters unsharded needs about 70 GB per GPU on top of state, so OOM is very likely.

hypotheses.mechanism: TF32 for fp32 matmuls
hypotheses.rationale: The model is bf16, so only fp32 paths are affected: the router or gating in fp32, possibly the loss and the conv fallback. Small.

hypotheses.mechanism: Disable NVLS for the collectives
hypotheses.rationale: Across 2 nodes NVLS(-tree) uses buffers and SM-side work that can slow overlapped compute. Ring/tree may suit FSDP2 all-gather/reduce-scatter with compute overlap better. The comm phase is only 4.6%.

hypotheses.mechanism: More NCCL channels for inter-node FSDP collectives
hypotheses.rationale: More channels raise all-gather/reduce-scatter bandwidth over IB and shrink the exposed comm. They also take more SMs away from overlapped compute, so the net effect could be slightly negative.

Halves backward recompute. Holding ~20 extra layers of activations is borderline after sharded states and the large-vocab logits on 80 GB, and fits better with Liger.
~2.2B params per rank under FSDP2; a fused Adam kernel cuts the optimizer step versus foreach. Small share of the step at 4k tokens x2.
Varying all-gather/logit buffer sizes near the 77 GiB limit cause fragmentation and allocator retries. Expandable segments avoid them; neutral if there is no pressure.
HF+FSDP2 compile of a 40-layer model with GQA/MoE-like paths risks graph breaks and long compile. Needs a per-host inductor cache on 2 nodes.
Amortizes the optimizer step over 2 micro-batches per token. FSDP still reduce-scatters each micro-batch. This changes the global batch, so it is a semantics change.
Training is bf16, so tf32 only touches the few fp32 matmuls (router or upcast paths). Negligible on H100.
FSDP collectives on 2 nodes are IB-limited and mostly overlapped. Measured IB 2-node weak scaling is ~0.98-1.0, so more channels add little.
A 35B model step at 4k tokens dwarfs data loading, and 2 workers already keep up. Watch for epoch-boundary stalls when comparing.
NVLS speeds intra-node reduce-scatter/all-gather, but 2-node collectives are bounded by IB. Disabling frees a little memory and may cost slightly.
No reshard keeps every layer's full bf16 params (~70 GB for 35B) from forward to backward, on top of sharded states, which exceeds 77 GiB. IB all-gather is cheap anyway.
Halves tokens per step while per-step FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter and optimizer cost stay the same. Lower GEMM M and worse comm amortization.

assessment.why: With a 248k vocab at seq 4096, the logits plus their fp32 copy and gradient are about 8-10 GB. Fused cross-entropy removes them and their memory traffic. Main risk: Liger may not support this model type.

Removes about half of the recompute (roughly 12% of step FLOPs). But each uncheckpointed layer holds about 0.75 GB at s=4096 (ffn 17408), so this adds about 24 GB. That is tight on 77 GB. Values 3 and 4 likely run out of memory.
Each GPU updates about 1.7B sharded params on 3.35 TB/s HBM. The fused step saves tens of ms against a step of about 2-3 s. FSDP2 DTensor is supported.
Possible gain from fusing elementwise ops. Risks: FSDP2 plus checkpointing graph breaks, compile time, and on 2 nodes a shared inductor/triton cache race. Needs per-host cache dirs.
FSDP2 all-gather buffers and large-vocab logits fragment the caching allocator. Expandable segments avoid cudaMalloc retries and free headroom for selective checkpointing.
NVLS speeds intra-node collectives on the H100 NVSwitch. Inter-node IB at about 354 GB/s is not the bottleneck either way. Disabling it mainly frees about 1 GB of NCCL buffers.
FLUX 11.9B gained from ZeRO-2 over IB. Here, keeping full 27B params unsharded costs at least 54 GB bf16 per GPU on top of about 27 GB of sharded states, which exceeds 77 GB.
Training is bf16, so almost no fp32 matmuls are left for TF32 to accelerate.
Step time is several seconds per 4k-token sample per GPU. Two workers already hide loading. Measure the median step to avoid epoch-boundary stalls.
Each batch is just one tensor of 4096 token ids, so the H2D copy is negligible either way.

calls.memory_note: Estimated baseline is about 42-50 GB of 77.3 GB per GPU: about 27 GB of FSDP-sharded fp32 states across 16 GPUs, plus about 10 GB of large-vocab logits, checkpointed activations and buffers; that leaves room for Liger but only marginal room for every_n_layers=2 (about +24 GB), and none for no-reshard or every_n_layers 3-4.

findings.issue: The gated-delta-net layers run the depthwise causal conv1d through the PyTorch reference path (nn.Conv1d with padding, slice, then silu) because causal_conv1d is not installed. This is a slow cuDNN depthwise conv on a wide channel dimension. With gradient checkpointing every layer it runs forward tw
Liger kernels are off. RMSNorm, SwiGLU and RoPE run unfused. Cross-entropy materializes fp32 logits over the ~248k vocabulary for 4096 tokens per rank, a large memory-bound cost inside compute.
Gradient checkpointing recomputes every decoder layer, adding roughly one extra forward to the compute phase. Memory headroom on 80 GB with batch 1 x 4096 likely allows checkpointing fewer layers.
Element-wise work in the model runs as many separate kernels in eager mode.
AdamW runs as the foreach (non-fused) implementation; this is the optimizer phase, about 1.8% of the update.
Any fp32 matmuls (e.g. the fp32 parts of the gated-delta-net and loss paths) run without TF32.
Each step re-gathers and frees FSDP2 shards, so the caching allocator sees varying block sizes and may fragment.

hypotheses.mechanism: selective activation checkpointing: keep the GEMM and SDPA outputs, recompute only the element-wise work
hypotheses.rationale: Compute is 93% of the update. With every layer checkpointed, each layer's forward runs twice, which is about 25% of compute, and most of that is GEMM. Saving the mm/addmm and SDPA outputs (non-reentrant checkpoint with a selective policy) removes the GEMM part of the recompute. The arithmetic is unchanged. It costs roughly 0.5 GB per layer of saved projections, about 30 GB for 64 layers on top of

hypotheses.mechanism: checkpoint fewer decoder layers (less recompute)
hypotheses.rationale: Halving the checkpointed layers removes about half of the extra forward, roughly 12% of compute. The cost is activations of the un-checkpointed layers, about 1-1.3 GB each at 4096 tokens with hidden 5120 / ffn 17408, so about 40 GB. With about 27 GB of sharded 27B states this is tight on 77 GB.

hypotheses.mechanism: torch.compile the model (fuse element-wise work), with per-host inductor/triton caches
hypotheses.rationale: Unfused RMSNorm, gating, SiLU and residual element-wise work runs in eager mode and is recomputed under checkpointing. The patch only enables compile: a shared-filesystem cache races across the 2 hosts (rule B18). Graph breaks around fla Triton ops and FSDP2 hooks limit the gain and add crash risk.

hypotheses.mechanism: cudnn.benchmark for the fallback depthwise causal conv1d
hypotheses.rationale: The gated-delta-net layers run nn.Conv1d (depthwise, kernel 4, wide channel dim) through cuDNN with the heuristic algorithm. assessment.why: Vocab 248k at seq 4096: fused linear CE skips about 2 GB of bf16 logits plus fp32 copies (about 8 GB peak) and some memory-bound passes. Risk: an unsupported arch makes it a no-op.
Halves recompute (about 12% of FLOPs). It adds about 0.85 GB per uncheckpointed layer, roughly 27 GB, which is tight on 77 GiB. Fits mainly with Liger. Gain is reduced if the step is IB-bound.
The fused Adam step over about 1.7B sharded params per GPU (27B over 16 GPUs) is a small share of a multi-second FSDP step. DTensor fused support is needed in this torch.

Elementwise fusion in a 27B dense model on H100. Risks: graph breaks with FSDP2 plus checkpointing, and an inductor cache race on shared FS across 2 nodes. Kernels are GEMM-dominated, so the gain is small.
Allocator only. It cuts fragmentation from the large variable logits/all-gather buffers. It can lower peak memory and stop allocator retries, but brings no throughput gain unless memory is near OOM.
On 2 nodes the FSDP collectives are limited by IB (about 47 GB/s per GPU), not NVLink. Disabling NVLS frees some memory and may slightly slow the intra-node phase.
bf16 mixed precision already runs the GEMMs in bf16. TF32 only touches the rare fp32 matmuls.
About 4k tokens per GPU per multi-second step, so input cost is negligible. Epoch-boundary worker respawn stalls should be excluded via the median step.
The token batch is tiny (4096 ids), so pinned vs pageable copy time does not matter.
About 43 uncheckpointed layers is roughly 36 GB of activations on top of about 47 GB baseline. That likely OOMs on 77 GiB, even with Liger.
About 48 uncheckpointed layers is roughly 41 GB of activations on top of about 47 GB baseline, which exceeds 77 GiB.
FLUX 12B gained from ZeRO-2 on 2 IB nodes, but 27B keeps about 54 GB unsharded bf16 params plus about 27 GB sharded states, which exceeds 77 GiB.

calls.memory_note: An estimated ~47 GB of 77.3 GiB is used per GPU (fp32 sharded params/grads/Adam ~27 GB over 16 GPUs plus ~10 GB vocab-248k logits peak and buffers), leaving ~30 GB: enough for Liger and maybe every_n_layers=2, not for no-reshard FSDP or sparser checkpointing.

findings.issue: Every GatedDeltaNet layer in the Qwen3.5 linear-attention blocks runs the reference causal conv1d path, as the job log reports. That path is nn.Conv1d with padding=k-1 over the full packed sequence, then a slice back to seq_len, then a separate SiLU, all over a (B, conv_dim, 4096) bf16 activation. W

Full activation recompute: gradient checkpointing on every layer (every_n_layers=1) repeats the whole forward inside backward, roughly 25-33% of compute. Checkpointing fewer layers removes part of that recompute if memory allows. Memory headroom is unknown because no memory receipt is shown.

Unfused element-wise work: RMSNorm, SwiGLU and RoPE run as separate kernels. The cross-entropy over the large Qwen3.5 vocabulary materializes the full fp32 logits for 4096 tokens. Liger's fused kernels and fused linear cross-entropy reach this work, provided liger 0.8.5 patches this architecture.
Eager execution leaves the remaining element-wise chains unfused and adds launch overhead per op. torch_compile reaches this. Graph breaks are likely around the fla Triton ops.
The optimizer step runs the per-parameter foreach AdamW (45 ms, 1.8% of the update). The fused AdamW kernel shortens it.
fp32 matmuls, for example in the gated-delta gating and norm paths, run without TF32 tensor cores.

FSDP2 re-gathers parameters for backward after resharding them in forward. Comm is only 2.3% of the update and is mostly overlapped. It can be shortened by keeping parameters unsharded after forward (fsdp_v2_noreshard.json) and by NVLS collectives (NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE).

hypotheses.mechanism: expandable_segments allocator: less fragmentation and fewer cudaMalloc retries under FSDP2 all-gather buffers

hypotheses.mechanism: torch.compile: fuse the remaining element-wise chains (norms, SwiGLU, RoPE, gating) and cut launch overhead
hypotheses.rationale: MFU is about 36% of the measured bf16 throughput, so non-GEMM work is substantial. Compile fuses the element-wise chains. hypotheses.mechanism: TF32 tensor cores for the remaining fp32 matmuls

hypotheses.mechanism: disable NVLS collectives (use ring/tree all-gather and reduce-scatter)

assessment.why: Full recompute costs ~21% on H200. 27B full-FT states are ~54 GB/GPU; no-ckpt activations at 4k add ~55-65 GB, plus ~10 GB of 248k-vocab logits. Tight on 140 GB; liger helps.
H200 rule: always compile (FSDP2 +24%). HF Trainer adds graph breaks with FSDP2 + checkpointing + overhead (H6), so the gain is smaller. Recompiles or crashes are possible.
The 248k vocab makes fp32 logits and CE large; fused linear-CE cuts memory and time. Glue kernels matter on H200 (H15). Risk: model_type not supported, which means no effect.
mbs 1 at 4k underfills GEMMs. Per-token FSDP gather and optimizer overhead halve. Fits easily with checkpointing on. Doubles global batch unless paired with GA 1.
Saves one all-gather per layer in backward (NCCL ~28% under FSDP2). Keeps ~54 GB of unsharded bf16 params resident, roughly 108 GB if fp32. OOM risk.
Fused AdamW over a 3.4B-param shard per GPU trims a memory-bound step of tens of ms against a ~5 s step. Small but above 0.14% noise.
Alone it halves tokens per optimizer step, so the optimizer cost is amortized over less work. Positive only when paired with mbs 2 to keep the global batch.
Mainly reduces fragmentation. It helps the no-ckpt or noreshard configs fit rather than speeding the reference.
The bf16 run's matmuls are already bf16. TF32 only touches the rare fp32 matmuls.
Disabling NVLS frees some memory but can slow intra-node AG/RS on NVSwitch. Effect is likely within noise to slightly negative.
A ~5 s step at 8k tokens per GPU is not input-bound. 2 workers already suffice.
Batches are tiny (mbs 1 x 4k tokens), so the H2D copy is negligible next to multi-second steps.

calls.memory_note: Assuming full fine-tuning under FSDP2, sharded fp32 params, grads and Adam take ~54 GB/GPU. With checkpointing, activations plus 248k-vocab logits add ~15-25 GB, leaving about 60 GB of headroom. Turning checkpointing off (+55-65 GB) or no-reshard (+54 GB or more) pushes toward the 140 GB limit, so use liger with either one and do not combine them with each other or with mbs 2.

assessment.why: vocab 248320 x seq 4096 gives ~1e9 logits per micro-batch; fused linear CE avoids the bf16/fp32 logits and saves time and GBs. No-op risk if the model family is not patched
Same global batch; larger GEMMs and half the FSDP gathers per sample on 740-TFLOPS H100. Doubles activations and logits on 77 GiB, so OOM risk is real unless liger is on
Fast H100 GEMMs make elementwise/norm overhead a larger share; compile fuses it. Risks: graph breaks or recompiles under FSDP2 and HF, and overlap with liger fusions
Skips the backward all-gather; that comm is mostly overlapped over NVLink 450 GB/s. Costs about 17 GB extra (unsharded bf16 8.95B) on 77 GiB
Fused AdamW over about 1.1B sharded params per rank cuts kernel launches. The step runs once per 2 micro-batches, so the gain is small
Reduces fragmentation. It only speeds up a run near the 77 GiB limit (alloc retries); otherwise it enables bigger configs
Disabling NVLink SHARP frees some NCCL memory. FSDP collectives on 8x NVSwitch are mostly overlapped, so the effect is near zero, slightly negative
Training matmuls are bf16; TF32 only affects the few fp32 matmuls
Alone this halves the global batch, so there are twice the optimizer steps and reduce-scatters per token. Only useful paired with mbs 2
About 0.7 s+ GPU step per 4k-token micro-batch; 2 workers already keep up with tokenized text
Batch is a few KB-MB of token ids; the H2D copy is negligible either way

calls.memory_note: Fully sharded fp32 states take about 18 GB per GPU of 77.3 GiB. Activations and the vocab-248k logits (several GB per 4k sequence) dominate the rest. Liger frees the logits, which should leave room for noreshard's ~17 GB but makes adding mbs 2 on top tight.

hypotheses.mechanism: regional torch.compile of the decoder RMSNorm and SwiGLU MLP forwards (element-wise fusion of the fp32 norm chain and of act*up)
hypotheses.rationale: Eager RMSNorm moves about 0.5 GB per call forward and about twice that backward. 130 norm calls per update cost about 50-65 ms, and the SwiGLU element-wise work costs another 10-20 ms. Inductor fuses each into one or two kernels per direction. With inline_inbuilt_nn_modules all layer instances share one graph. FSDP2 hooks stay on the decoder layers, outside the compiled regions. The fla gated norm
hypotheses.site: Qwen3_5RMSNorm.forward (about 65 calls per micro-batch on 4096x4096 activations, upcast to fp32 and run as about 6 separate eager kernels, with fp32 intermediates saved for backward) and Qwen3_5MLP.forward (silu(gate)*up on 4096x12288 as separate kernels). Together they are a memory-bound slice of the 1486 ms compute phase.

hypotheses.mechanism: whole-model torch.compile via the Trainer knob
hypotheses.rationale: Fuses every element-wise op in the dense decoder: norms, SwiGLU, rotary, attention output gate, gated-delta-net gating math, residual adds, and possibly the reference causal-conv epilogue. Compile time falls in warmup steps 1-10, outside the measured window. The risks are graph breaks at the fla Triton autograd functions, recompiles, and FSDP2 plus compile issues, so feasibility is moderate.

hypotheses.mechanism: cudnn.benchmark autotuning for the fixed-shape depthwise conv1d of the reference causal_conv1d fallback
hypotheses.rationale: The input shape is constant, so benchmarking pays from the first steps. bf16 depthwise conv backward under heuristic algorithm choice is often several times slower than the best algorithm. This is a one-line change. It is redundant once the queued fla causal-conv patch lands, but it stands alone and composes harmlessly with it.
hypotheses.site: nn.Conv1d (depthwise, groups=channels, seq 4096) in the gated-delta-net layers, taken because causal_conv1d is missing (job log note). Forward and the slow depthwise weight-grad backward run through cuDNN's default heuristic.

hypotheses.mechanism: put cuDNN SDPA first in the attention backend priority (fallback to flash and the others kept)
hypotheses.rationale: Attention is only about 2% of the FLOPs here: 8 layers at d=256 are about 8 TFLOP per update per GPU. cuDNN on H100 is faster than FA2 at large head dims when supported. If d=256 or enable_gqa is not supported, the call falls back and the gain is zero.
hypotheses.site: F.scaled_dot_product_attention in the full-attention layers (every 4th layer, head_dim 256, GQA 16/4, causal, seq 4096), now on the FA2 flash backend.

hypotheses.mechanism: micro-batch 2 without accumulation: one FSDP gather and reduce-scatter cycle per update instead of two, and fewer, larger kernels
hypotheses.rationale: Global batch stays at 16 (8 x 2 x 1). This halves the per-update parameter all-gathers and gradient reduce-scatters under reshard and halves the per-micro-step launch overhead. Activations and logits roughly double (about 36+6 GiB more) against a 12.8 GiB margin, so it is likely OOM unless activation checkpointing is already on.

hypotheses.mechanism: expandable_segments allocator to avoid fragmentation and cudaMalloc retries near the memory cap
hypotheses.rationale: The estimated peak is about 64.5 of 77.3 GiB, with large variable-size blocks (4 GB fp32 logits and FSDP unsharded buffers). That pattern fragments the caching allocator and can trigger cache flushes. Expandable segments remove that cost and part of the residual.

hypotheses.mechanism: disable NVLS (NVLink SHARP) collectives for FSDP all-gather and reduce-scatter
hypotheses.rationale: The comm phase is only 32 ms exposed. NVLS buffer registration and setup can add memory and sometimes latency for the many medium-size per-layer FSDP collectives. Ring or tree NVLink paths may overlap compute better. The gain is bounded by the 2% comm share.

hypotheses.mechanism: TF32 for the remaining fp32 matmuls and convs
hypotheses.rationale: The model runs in bf16, so only the few fp32 GEMMs and convs (gating parameters, any fp32 paths in the linear-attention projections) benefit. The effect is small but cheap and safe.

hypotheses.mechanism: more dataloader workers to hide host-side batch assembly
hypotheses.rationale: Data is memmapped int32 rows at 4096 tokens, so loading is trivial. Only part of the 70 ms residual could be input-related, and the expected effect is near zero.

hypotheses.mechanism: put cuDNN SDPA first in the attention backend priority for the full-attention layers; flash, efficient and math stay as fallbacks (re-proposed on c4, the c0 patch was never tested)
hypotheses.rationale: Only about a quarter of the layers use softmax attention, at seq 4096 with head_dim 256. Their flash forward and backward are roughly 1-2% of compute, and cuDNN on H100 is typically 10-30% faster on those calls. If cuDNN rejects the GQA or head-dim-256 calls, it falls back to flash and the change is a no-op. Rule sw-sdpa-priority: set the priority rather than forcing one backend, so nothing crashe
hypotheses.site: torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention in the full-attention layers (transformers sdpa_attention_forward, causal, no mask, GQA 16/4) inside the compute phase (1486 ms, 92% of the update)

hypotheses.mechanism: explicit FSDP2 forward and backward prefetch between consecutive decoder blocks, so the next block's all-gather is issued before the current block computes
hypotheses.rationale: With noreshard, backward needs no all-gather. Forward still gathers each block at its pre-hook, twice per update (two micro-batches). When the CPU is not far ahead, as happens with a hybrid model's many small kernels, that gather is exposed. Explicit prefetch issues it one block earlier. Comm is only 2% of the update, so the gain is capped near 2%. The arithmetic is unchanged.
hypotheses.site: accelerate fsdp2_prepare_model / FSDP2 per-block all-gathers: comm phase 32 ms exposed, plus part of the 70 ms residual from waits at block starts with mb=1 and many small GatedDeltaNet kernels

hypotheses.mechanism: turn off activation recompute (HF gradient_checkpointing or FSDP activation_checkpointing) if the frozen launch enables it; no-op otherwise
hypotheses.rationale: The CLI flags are not visible. Compute is 92% of the update at roughly 300 effective TFLOPs per GPU. If full recompute is on, removing it saves about a quarter of compute (~20%). Activations at mb=1, seq 4096 (accounting: ~36 GiB) fit beside the ~17 GiB sharded state with Liger's fused cross entropy. If recompute is off, the patch changes nothing. hypotheses.site: TrainingArguments.__post_init__ (gradient_checkpointing / fsdp_config activation_checkpointing), which decides whether every decoder block's forward is recomputed in backward

hypotheses.mechanism: raise the Python GC thresholds so generation-2 collections over the many parameter and tensor objects stop stalling some updates
hypotheses.rationale: Occasional generation-2 collections pause the launching thread for tens of milliseconds and appear as stalled updates rather than a slower median. Raising the thresholds makes them rare. The gain is judged by the mean, and its size is bounded by the residual phase.

assessment.why: Full recompute costs about 21% on H200, the same tax as on H20. With 141 GB and the model sharded 8 ways, activations at 4k, mbs1 and 32 layers fit (~30-40 GB).
HF+FSDP2 went 7004->8684 when compiled (+24%), and compile helps more on H200 than on H20. Risks are graph breaks with HF FSDP2 and checkpointing, and an unfamiliar model class.
A 248k vocab makes the logits/CE large, and fused linear-CE plus RMSNorm/SwiGLU cut glue kernels, which matter on H200. Liger may not support this model class.
Removes the backward all-gather. NCCL is about 28% of FSDP2 kernel time on H200, and the unsharded params (~18-36 GB) fit in the headroom.
A larger micro-batch amortizes FSDP comm, launch overhead and the optimizer per token, and memory allows it. Note this doubles the global batch unless GA is set to 1.
The optimizer step on ~1.1B sharded params per GPU is a few % of a ~1.5 s step. Fused vs foreach saves part of that.
Halves the global batch, so the optimizer step and its overhead are amortized over half the tokens. This is only neutral when paired with mbs 2.
The GEMMs run in bf16 under autocast, and only stray fp32 matmuls are affected. This is below or near the 0.14% noise.
Reduces fragmentation and allocator churn. There is plenty of headroom, so speed changes little; it is useful mainly if mbs2 or no-recompute nears the memory limit.
At ~1-1.5 s per micro-step with 4k tokens, 2 workers already keep pace with tokenized data.
The H2D input is a tiny int tensor per step, so pinning is irrelevant at this scale.
Disabling NVSwitch SHARP may slightly slow FSDP all-gather and reduce-scatter. Comm is mostly overlapped, so the effect is near noise.

calls.memory_note: The sharded fp32 params, grads and Adam states take about 18 GB per GPU, so dropping recompute (~30-40 GB of activations plus ~10 GB of 248k-vocab logits) and keeping params unsharded (~18-36 GB) should still leave about 40 GB free of 141 GB.

assessment.why: Full recompute costs about 21% on H200. At 8.95B with FSDP8 at s4k and mbs1, no-recompute activations plus about 8-12 GB of 248k-vocab logits fit easily in 141 GB.
HF+FSDP2 went from 7004 to 8684 when compiled on H200 (+24%), and glue kernels matter there. Risk: graph breaks or compile failure in HF with recompute or a new model type.
Skips the backward all-gather (NCCL is about 28% of FSDP2 time on H200). Keeping bf16 params unsharded costs about 18 GB per GPU, which fits in 141 GB.
Fused linear cross-entropy avoids materialising 4096x248k logits; RMSNorm and SwiGLU fusions cut glue time. Gain is smaller if the model type is unpatched or compile also runs.
Bigger GEMMs and fewer launches and collectives per token on an overhead-heavy H200. Memory fits. Global batch doubles unless GA is set to 1 (B12 holds for gbs 16 with DP8).
A fused AdamW step over about 1.1B sharded params per GPU saves tens of ms in a roughly 1 s step. It works with FSDP2 DTensor on recent torch.
Alone, this halves the tokens per optimizer step, so the optimizer and reduce-scatter amortise worse. It is only neutral when paired with mbs 2 to keep gbs 16.
Disabling NVSwitch SHARP collectives on a single 8-GPU node can slow FSDP all-gather and reduce-scatter, which are a large share of the step on H200. It frees a little memory.
bf16 autocast already covers the GEMMs; only stray fp32 matmuls are affected. Store noise is 0.14%.
Reduces fragmentation and cudaMalloc retries. Ample headroom on 141 GB means little speed effect; it helps if no-recompute or mbs 2 gets close to the limit.
Steps of about 1 s with 8k tokens per GPU are not input-bound with 2 workers on pre-tokenised data.
Token-ID batches are tiny (KB), so pageable versus pinned host-to-device copies are negligible against a step of about 1 s.

assessment.why: Full recompute costs about 21% on H200. 141 GB holds the activations of an 8.95B model at s4k mbs1 (about 25 GB) plus the 248k-vocab logits, so recompute can be dropped.
Rule: always compile on H200. HF+FSDP2 went 7004 -> 8684 (+24%), and glue kernels are a large share of step time. Risk: graph breaks or failures with FSDP2 and checkpointing.
The 248k vocab makes the logits and cross-entropy heavy; fused linear-CE plus fused RMSNorm/SwiGLU cut glue kernels and memory. Risk: this model type may not be supported by Liger.
FSDP2 NCCL share is 28% on H200. Not resharding skips the backward all-gather (and the recompute one). It costs about 18-36 GB of unsharded params, which fits in 141 GB.
Larger GEMMs amortise the FSDP collectives. But with GA 2 the global batch rises from 16 to 32, a recipe change. It is tight in memory if recompute is also dropped.
A fused AdamW step over a 1.1B-param shard per GPU saves kernel launches. It is a small part of a step with gbs 16 x 4k tokens.
With 141 GB there is little fragmentation pressure, so no speed change is expected. It only matters if the run gets close to OOM.
The GEMMs run in bf16. TF32 affects only fp32 matmuls, which are rare here.
Steps are multiple seconds and the input is pre-tokenized, so 2 workers already keep up.
Host-to-device copies of the token IDs are negligible next to the step time.
NVLS speeds up NVSwitch collectives, but FSDP reduce-scatter/all-gather mostly overlap with compute. Disabling it frees a little memory and may slow communication slightly.
With mbs 1 the global batch halves to 8, so the optimizer step and gradient reduce-scatter are amortised over half as many tokens. It is neutral only if paired with mbs 2.

calls.memory_note: FSDP2 shards the fp32 params, grads and Adam states of the 8.95B model to about 18 GB per GPU. Without recompute, activations plus the 248k-vocab logits should peak around 60-80 GB (less with Liger's fused CE), leaving headroom on 141 GB for no-reshard but tight for mbs 2.

findings.issue: Site: the GatedDeltaNet forward in transformers.models.qwen3_5 (and qwen3_next) modeling, the short causal conv over mixed_qkv. Evidence: the job log note says causal_conv1d_fn falls back to the reference PyTorch implementation because causal_conv1d is missing. That path is a depthwise nn.Conv1d plu
fp32 matmul paths (the logits/loss upcast and other fp32 ops) run without TF32.
Gradient checkpointing recomputes the whole forward pass. A 9B model sharded by FSDP over 8x141 GiB at micro-batch 1 and sequence length 4096 likely fits without it.
Unfused RMSNorm, SwiGLU and cross-entropy (large-vocab logits materialized). Liger kernels fuse them.
Micro-batch 1 with 2 accumulation steps means two forward/backward passes and two FSDP gather/reduce rounds per update. Batch 2 with accumulation 1 keeps the global batch at 16.
The for-each AdamW step is 1.5% of the update; the fused AdamW removes most of it.
